  peak_rss_gb: 14.8
  license_token_hours: 1.15
```

The `COMPLETED` status and zero exit code describe execution, while the negative timing slack reports a violation under the recorded constraints. These statements are compatible: the analysis completed and found a problem. The raw report reference lets a reviewer inspect which paths and conditions produced that result. Similarly, the subsystem power value is an estimate under the identified activity and library assumptions; it does not establish that the complete Lighthouse system meets its power budget. The cost fields describe resources consumed by this attempt, independently of whether the candidate met its requirements.

Records also support later attempts to reproduce the work. ACM artifact review guidelines distinguish *repeatability* (same team, same setup), *reproducibility* (different team, same setup), and *replicability* (different team, different setup) [@ACM2020ArtifactReview]. A record supplies information for these activities, but carrying them out also requires access to the artifacts and an executable procedure. The Popper convention similarly emphasizes preserving executable evaluation workflows [@JimenezEtAl2017PopperConvention].

Even with the same recorded inputs, host time or returned results may vary for the reasons discussed in @sec-incremental-churn-dispersion. Lineage identifies how artifacts were produced; references to behavioral checks show what was tested, not what hashes alone prove. The record makes these distinctions available to later analysis. Applying them to a prospective study shows how the environment's rules and its execution history fit together.

## Mobile XR Subsystem Evaluation Environment {#sec-mobile-xr-evaluation}

Applying these tool boundaries and execution contracts to the prospective mobile XR SoC study connects runtime policy to the intended design constraints. This illustration assumes a candidate organization with an NPU array ($16 \times 16$), dual LPDDR5X channels, Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) interconnects, UPF power domains, and L2 cache capacities ($2\text{--}4\text{ MiB}$) under a 3\ W thermal design power (TDP) envelope on a TSMC N3E process. The NPU is one possible Lighthouse compute organization; this environment example does not select it over other organizations. The run specification fixes what would be allowed before any tool invocation (@tbl-environment-contract).

| **Run category** | **Prospective XR SoC co-design study run specification** |
| --- | --- |
| **Candidates and fixed state** | Only `l2.capacity` varies among 2\ MiB, 3\ MiB, and 4\ MiB. The $16 \times 16$ NPU topology, memory arbitration, RISC-V CPU cores, NoC, software binary, XR workload trace, and remaining cache-policy parameters stay fixed. Capacity determines the corresponding static random-access memory (SRAM) organization under those fixed inputs. Candidates retain SRAM, NPU tile, LPDDR5X, UPF domain, and TSMC N3E identity. |
| **Translation and identity** | Parameters serialize into an analytical SRAM model under declared process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) conditions and into the inputs required by gem5/Ramulator 2/Verilator/SCALE-Sim. Power estimates require a separately identified power model or analysis engine, its activity inputs, and any UPF power intent that engine consumes. Schema, wrapper, parser, tool versions, container digest, and seeds retain explicit identity. |
| **Order and dispatch** | Analytical screening executes first. Cycle-level gem5/Ramulator 2 simulations dispatch only when screening reports valid area $\le 1.5\text{ mm}^2$ and access latency $\le 2.5\text{ ns}$. |
| **Matched work and limits** | Baseline and alternatives run under matched conditions. Budget: three screening runs, maximum four cycle-level attempts. Deadlines enforced; execution stops when work completes or budget expires. |
| **Failures and recovery** | Operational failures, timeouts, and parser errors remain distinct. Recovery retries link to parents, charge against budget, and regenerate clean workspaces from fixed state. |
| **Containment and reuse** | Least-privilege access to tools and paths. Quarantines unconfirmed terminations. Cache reuse requires exact matching of candidate, conditions, and tool/library hashes. |
| **Returns, cost, and lineage** | Retains SRAM/NPU area, latency, energy; frame records, memory traffic, NPU multiply-accumulate (MAC) utilization, subsystem power; raw logs, parsed outputs, hashes, costs, and parent–child lineage. |
| **Decisions left outside** | Environment does not decide measurement validity, comparative superiority, or candidate advancement. |
: **Prospective run specifications define permitted work before execution.** Request schemas, translations, state pinning, failure recovery, and budgets are fixed prior to invocation. {#tbl-environment-contract tbl-colwidths="[24,76]"}

Read as a whole, the specification fixes a design path before any return arrives: screening, then conditional cycle-level dispatch, then a planned repeat. What a return may change about that plan is decided outside the environment, which is why the last row exists. Consider an illustrative execution trace under this specification (@sec-running-the-loop records the study's actual project status). The evaluation would begin with three analytical screening runs: a 2\ MiB baseline ($1.2\text{ mm}^2$, 2.1\ ns), 3\ MiB ($1.4\text{ mm}^2$, 2.4\ ns), and 4\ MiB ($1.7\text{ mm}^2$, 2.8\ ns). The 4\ MiB candidate violates the area and latency thresholds, suppressing dependent cycle-level dispatch. The surviving candidates (2\ MiB and 3\ MiB) enter cycle-level simulation within the four-attempt budget. Were a setup failure to interrupt the 3\ MiB run, the specification charges a clean reset and retry against that same budget, followed by the planned repeat, consuming the remaining attempts. Downstream verification in @sec-feedback-verification-trust qualifies whether such returns support advancing the candidate.

## Open Questions

The chapter specifies what a harness must preserve, but leaves open how economically it can establish execution completeness, reset state, and the effects of upstream change.

- **How can a harness establish that a tool performed every requested check?** A clean exit code and a parseable report can leave requested corners or analysis stages unaccounted for. Retaining the complete log preserves clues, but the tool may not expose enough information to establish what it skipped. The unresolved problem is how to test execution completeness against the request across opaque tools and changing report formats. Even a complete account of execution would leave the validity of the selected checks, including their treatment of voltage droop,[^fn-voltage-droop-c06] to downstream qualification.

- **How do you ensure hardware emulation testbeds do not carry state from prior runs?** Accelerated FPGA and hardware emulation platforms can retain DRAM buffer state, PCIe registers, and memory contents across asynchronous invocations. Reinitialization must cover all state that can affect the measurement, including external memory and host-side state; reloading a bitstream or issuing a soft reset is insufficient unless it meets that requirement. The research problem is to verify the declared initialization without paying unnecessary reinitialization cost on every run.

- **How much running work can a harness preserve when upstream interfaces change?** A long synthesis or emulation run may still be evaluating a frozen revision when an upstream RTL interface or compiler pass changes. Aborting on every commit wastes work; retaining every return risks using a result whose assumptions no longer apply. Dependency graphs identify changed inputs, but do not by themselves establish which results remain valid, especially when a local edit changes physical placement or routing elsewhere. The unresolved problem is to determine which work must be repeated while preserving the useful results and costs of the earlier revision.

## Summary

An environment lets an architect determine, for every attempt, which candidate was requested, whether it ran, which state the tool inherited, what warnings it returned, and whether a retry repeated the same work. Setup fixes the inputs and tool contracts; runtime preserves those identities as work queues, executes, fails, or resumes. The resulting execution records make generated candidates and later revisions traceable across tool paths without turning a completed run into a design judgment.

::: {.callout-takeaways}
- **Typed wrappers before every launch.** Validate the request against frozen contracts, translate parameters exactly, parse returns into typed metrics, and keep the unclassified log lines the parser did not recognize.
- **Containment and license pooling.** Isolate mutable tool state, restrict access, confirm termination when a lease expires, and manage shared licenses. Keep restricted PDK collateral within its permitted compute boundary.
- **One execution record per authorized request/attempt.** Bind identity, pinned state, all attached backend executions, returns, lineage, and cost into the record. Retain refusals and failures; give retries linked records of their own.
- **Repeated-run budgeting over lucky seeds.** Fund repeated executions for randomized stages and retain every seed, thread count, condition, return, and cost. Reuse after an upstream change requires checking which dependencies remain valid.
- **Execution is not qualification.** The harness records what ran and what returned; whether a return supports a measurement, a comparison, or a candidate's advancement is decided downstream.
:::

@sec-feedback-verification-trust takes the execution records these environments return and asks what claims their measurements can support.

[^fn-sandboxing-kubernetes-c06]: **The orchestration parallel**: A correct tool script does not by itself control the state of concurrent or interrupted runs. Containers and workflow schedulers provide useful mechanisms for software execution, but an architecture environment must also coordinate tool-specific checkpoints, shared CAD licenses, and restricted design inputs. The harness performs this coordination for generated requests as well as requests written by an engineer.


[^fn-flexlm-c06]: **EDA Licensing**: Unmanaged tools using license managers (e.g., FlexLM) often silently block or hang in the queue when licenses are exhausted, emphasizing why wrappers with strict timeouts are critical.

[^fn-simpoint-smarts-c06]: **Simulation sampling**: SimPoint selects intervals based on program phases; SMARTS uses systematic sampling. Both reduce the amount of detailed execution that must be simulated. Their sampling and warmup assumptions remain part of the resulting performance estimate.


[^fn-physical-checkpoints-c06]: **Physical design checkpoints**: During chip layout, tools generate massive intermediate files. DEF (Design Exchange Format) stores the placement and routing of components. SPEF (Standard Parasitic Exchange Format) records the resistance and capacitance of the wires for timing analysis. GDSII is the final binary format representing the 2D shapes of the chip's masks, ultimately sent to the foundry for manufacturing.

[^fn-eda-formats-c06]: **EDA formats**: The physical design ecosystem relies on specialized file formats to separate concerns. A Liberty (`.lib`) file provides timing and power characterization for standard cells. A LEF (Library Exchange Format) file abstracts the physical dimensions and routing pins of a cell without revealing internal transistor layouts. UPF (Unified Power Format) describes power domains and voltage scaling logic, which are essential for low-power mobile SoCs.

[^fn-process-containment-c06]: **Process containment**: Commercial EDA tools can spawn background daemons and child processes. If a parent script is killed, live orphaned workers may continue consuming memory and holding licenses. They differ from zombie processes, which have exited and await reaping. Linux `cgroups` (control groups) keep a job's processes in a tracked group so the harness can terminate them together and confirm exit before reclaiming resources.

[^fn-false-path-c06]: **False-path waivers**: Timing exceptions that exclude specified paths from static timing checks when functional behavior or clock relationships justify doing so. The exception must be supported by the declared design and clock assumptions; a path's absence from simulation is not sufficient. Asynchronous clock-domain crossings still require appropriate synchronization and clock-domain-crossing checks.

[^fn-ir-drop-c06]: **IR drop**: The voltage reduction (V = I $\times$ R) that occurs as current travels through the resistive metal layers of the power delivery network, which can cause transistors to switch slower or fail entirely under heavy toggle activity.

[^fn-numa-c06]: **NUMA (Non-Uniform Memory Access)**: A computer memory design where memory access time depends on the memory location relative to the processor. Under NUMA, a processor can access its own local memory faster than non-local memory (memory local to another processor or shared between processors).
[^fn-seccomp-c06]: **seccomp (secure computing mode)**: A Linux kernel feature that restricts the system calls a process can make, reducing the exposed kernel surface. It is one component of containment, not a complete sandbox.
[^fn-voltage-droop-c06]: **Voltage droop**: A localized, temporary dip in supply voltage caused by sudden bursts of switching activity across many transistors simultaneously, which can induce timing failures not captured by static worst-case timing characterization.
[^fn-k-induction-c06]: **$k$-induction**: A formal proof method with two obligations. The base case establishes the property along executions from allowed initial states through the chosen depth. The inductive step establishes that, for any transition sequence admitted by the model, the property holding for $k$ consecutive states implies that it holds in the next state. Both obligations must succeed under the declared assumptions to establish the invariant beyond a bounded check.
